feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The candidate is the iteration-6 design (score 696.6, best so far) with two controller steps: kp 4.8 to 5.0 and kd 0.9 to 1.0. Geometry, ki 0.5, base_speed 1.3, sensor weights and line_loss last_direction are unchanged, so any difference comes from the gains. The evidence is iteration 6: oval finished 20 of 20 (steering_oscillation 0.232, max_error 0.0095), s-bend finished 20 of 20 (mean 2.42 s, steering_oscillation 0.334), and slalom never finished (progress 0.47, 1.25 line-loss events per run). Slalom is the main lost score. Across iterations 4 to 6, each paired rise in kp and kd cut s-bend max_error and line losses without an oval regression, so a further small step is a reasonable test. Two cautions. First, the claim that kp 5 with kd 0.3 overshoots comes from iteration 2, which had ki 0.02 and a different bias, so it is weak support for the damping ratio here; watch steering_oscillation directly. Second, kp 5.0 is the highest gain tested, and oval has the least margin on oscillation headroom (0.232 against a caution level near 0.35). Interpreting the next race: if oval stays at 20 of 20 with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.35, and slalom progress rises above 0.47 (or any slalom completion appears), keep kp 5.0 and kd 1.0 and consider a small base_speed step only if s-bend completion_time stays well under 2.8 s. If any oval run goes off track or oval steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.35, return kp to 4.8 and keep kd 1.0. If slalom progress is flat near 0.47 with line_loss_events still above 1 per run, the limit is sensor coverage rather than gain, so the next geometry test should widen the outer sensors (for example to x = ±0.04 m with weights rescaled to stay within [-2, 2]).
requested_changes: If oval stays at 20 of 20 with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.35 and slalom progress rises above 0.47, keep controller.kp at 5.0 and controller.kd at 1.0, since iteration 6 showed each paired gain step cut max_error and line losses without oval regression.

If any oval run goes off track or oval steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.35, set controller.kp back to 4.8 and keep controller.kd at 1.0, because the oval bends are the first place extra steering gain would show up as oscillation.

If slalom progress stays near 0.47 with line_loss_events still above 1 per run, leave the gains alone and test geometry.sensor_positions widened to x = ±0.04 m (rescale sensor_weights to stay within [-2, 2]), since iteration 6 losses point to sensor coverage on the tight alternating bends.
